top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a genuine new organising principle: time-reversal symmetry plus spin-orbit coupling gives a Z2 classification of band insulators with protected helical edge states, tested unambiguously by Molenkamp's HgTe quantum wells and left stable by about two decades of independent transport, photoemission and tunnelling work. The Kane, Mele, Molenkamp allocation pairs the jointly written founding theory with the first decisive experiment, and the citation is scoped to the 2D quantum spin Hall state so it does not claim the contested 3D materials priority or erase Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang. The 2016 prize covered topology in 1D chains and quantum Hall systems with broken time reversal, so the increment is distinct. P002 (optical lattice clocks, Katori and Ye) is a mature, cleanly attributed invention and a close second, but narrower in reach and its distinctness from the 2005 and 2012 prizes is something I cannot test independently. Any award is preferable to no award given two mature, well-attributed candidates.
recusal_note: No personal or institutional link to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori or Ye is apparent from my profile; my electronic-structure and band-theory background is close to the materials side of P001, so I flag possible subject bias and have discounted it.
